Definition: probably from G5443 through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid:--beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare G5083.
BiblicalUsage: Phylasso means to keep, to guard, to watch over what has been entrusted to you. Jesus blesses those who hear the word of God and keep it in Luke 11:28, and He says He kept His disciples in the Father's name in John 17:12. Paul charges Timothy to keep the good thing committed to him in 2 Timothy 1:14, and Jude ends by praising the God who is able to keep us from falling in Jude 1:24.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe keeping is a two-way promise: I keep His word, and He keeps me. My position is that obedience is not the price of His keeping — it is the proof of it.
